title: [performance] The scorecard says how long a landing waits from its report to the deploy that puts it live (the performance north star)
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-postgres/src/scorecard.rs (the control records the scorecard reads), crates/spawn-cli/src/scorecard/history.rs (the landings and their tasks) and measure.rs (`Counts`, `NAMES`, the dimensions, `lead_time`), web/src/scorecardFormat.ts and web/src/scorecard.ts (the Scorecard page's model).

The problem (owner, 2026-11-12 13:30; sync/roadmap-effects.md, "North-star and guardrail metrics", Performance). The performance line's north star is the time from "work reported" to "live": how long a finished change waits before the owner can use it, through judging, landing and deploy. No figure says it. The Scorecard's lead time runs from a task's assignment to its landing (1 h 24 min a landing over 7 days), and the deploy that follows is in no figure (about 8 min by hand). The record holds both ends: a task's `task.reported`, and each `deploy.finished` (`ok`, `head`), which ships the then-current main and so every landing before it.

Required behaviour.
(a) Every scope's `dimensions` on `/api/scorecard` carries `report_to_live`, in the same envelope as the others (`value`, `n`, `enough`, `better`, `previous`, `trend` and its parts):
- `value`: the median, by nearest rank as lead time takes it, over the window's landings (task landings: `task.landed`, or a review mission's accepting `task.reviewed`, as the scorecard counts them). For each landing, the time from its task's last `task.reported` before it landed to the first `deploy.finished` with `ok` true at or after the landing. A failed deploy ships nothing.
- `p90`: the same at 90.
- `n`: how many of the window's landings are live.
- `not_live`: how many have no such deploy yet. They are left out of value and p90.
- `better`: "lower".
- It is `enough` when at least the scorecard's `min_n` landings are live.
(b) web/src/scorecardFormat.ts exports `reportToLiveText(dimension)`: "<value in hours, one decimal> h from report to live (<n> landing[s])", with the parenthesis ending "; <not_live> not live yet" when not_live is above 0; null when the dimension or its value is missing. The module keeps loading with node alone.
(c) The Scorecard page shows report to live as a dimension card with that line, beside lead time. web/src/scorecard.ts lists the dimension (`DIMENSION_KEYS`, `DIMENSION_INFO` "Report to live", "per landing", said as a span).

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/081.sh. The history is seeded as the store holds it, hours before one fixed "now", and `spawn serve` answers. One mission and five tasks:
- T1: reported -10, accepted, landed -9.5, deploy ok -9 (1.0 h).
- T2: reported -8.5, rejected, reported -8, accepted, landed -7.4; a failed deploy at -7; deploy ok -6 (2.0 h, from its last report).
- T3: reported -5, landed -4.5. T4: reported -4.8, landed -4.2. One deploy ok at -4 ships both (1.0 h and 0.8 h).
- T5: reported -2, landed -1.5, no deploy since.
Checks:
- (1) through `GET /api/scorecard`: the fleet's report_to_live is {value 1.0 h, p90 2.0 h, n 4, not_live 1, better lower}, and mission 1's is the same;
- (2) under node, reportToLiveText gives "1.0 h from report to live (4 landings; 1 not live yet)" for it, "1.5 h from report to live (1 landing)" for one landing of 1.5 h with none waiting, and null for no value.
It fails with 1 on b4cda42e: there is no report_to_live, and scorecardFormat.ts has no reportToLiveText. (c), the card on the page, is read off a screenshot.

The product reason. This is the figure the performance line steers by: a change helps the owner only once it is live. Lead time stops at the landing and hides the deploy wait, so a slow or failing deploy would never show on the Scorecard. Monitoring only: no gate, integrator or deploy step reads it.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/, web/test/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green (043, 061, 062, 067 and 076 among them) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour: a scorecard unit test of report_to_live (a failed deploy, a re-report, a landing not live), a spawn-postgres test that the scorecard's records carry `task.reported` and `deploy.finished` through the real store, and a web/test test of reportToLiveText.
